---
title: "wraptool"
subtitle: "Credential-isolated MCP gateway for CLI tools"
---

**wraptool** is a Go-based [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/)
server that wraps CLI tools (`git`, `gcloud`, `kubectl`, ...) behind a
security whitelist, so AI coding assistants can use them without ever
seeing the underlying credentials.

## Why

AI coding assistants need CLI tools to be productive, but giving them
direct access exposes API keys, SSH keys, kubeconfigs, and service
account credentials to the model context. wraptool sits between the
assistant and the tools:

- **Credentials stay isolated** — wraptool runs on the **host** with the
  secrets; the assistant runs in an **isolated container** (user/mount
  namespace) that never mounts your `$HOME`, SSH keys, or tokens. Anything
  privileged (`git push`, private fetch, `gcloud`, `kubectl`) crosses the
  boundary only through wraptool's policed MCP tools.
- **Subcommand-level whitelisting** — allow `git commit` but deny
  `git push --force`, with flag-level granularity and value
  constraints. Deny always beats allow.
- **Auto-discovery** — wraptool parses `--help` output to generate
  MCP tool schemas with real descriptions, so the AI knows what each
  flag does.
- **Structured denial workflow** — when a command is denied, the AI
  can submit a capability request that an operator reviews and approves
  — from the **command line** (`wraptool requests`) or a browser-based
  **[Web UI](web-ui.qmd)** (approve/deny, live rule editing, tool-call audit).
- **One-command setup** — `wraptool up` in a repo starts the shared
  server, **auto-provisions** the assistant's MCP config (with the auth
  header), and drops you into the isolated container. No manual wiring.

## High-level architecture

The assistant lives in an isolated box with **no credentials**; secrets and
the privileged tools stay on the host, reachable only through the policy engine.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  subgraph box["🔒 Isolated container — no credentials"]
    ai[AI Coding<br/>Assistant]
    localgit[local git<br/>status / diff / commit]
  end

  subgraph host["Host — credentials live here"]
    wt[wraptool<br/>server]
    policy[Policy Engine<br/>deny &gt; allow &gt; constraints]
    exec[Sandboxed Exec<br/>+ credential scrub]
    cli[Privileged CLI<br/>git push / gcloud / kubectl]
    creds[(Credentials<br/>SSH keys · tokens · kubeconfig)]
    op[Operator review<br/>CLI + Web UI]
  end

  ai -- "MCP tool call<br/>Bearer auth" --> wt
  wt --> policy
  policy -- "allowed" --> exec
  exec --> cli
  cli -.-> creds
  exec -- "scrubbed output" --> wt
  wt -- "result" --> ai
  policy -- "denied" --> req[Capability<br/>request]
  req --> op
  op -- "approve / deny" --> policy

  style box fill:#eef,stroke:#3a3ad0
  style creds fill:#fee,stroke:#E60028
  style policy fill:#fef,stroke:#666
```

Local, non-privileged git runs inside the box; only credentialed operations
cross into wraptool. The container boundary is a user/mount namespace — your
`$HOME` and secrets are never shared in.
